prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode was rejecting requests whose Accept header only listed `application/json` (previously required both `application/json` AND `text/event-stream`). Both PRs relax webStandardStreamableHttp.ts's Accept-header validation to allow JSON-only clients. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode was rejecting requests whose Accept header only listed `application/json` (previously required both `application/json` AND `text/event-stream`). Both PRs relax webStandardStreamableHttp.ts's Accept-header validation to allow JSON-only clients. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 1996 implements a proper RFC 7231-style Accept header parser (acceptsMediaType): it splits entries on commas, strips per-entry parameters, explicitly excludes entries with q=0, and supports type/subtype wildcard matching. 2046 instead uses a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check with no q-value handling, which can false-positive on unrelated subtypes containing that substring (e.g. `application/json-patch+json`, `application/jsonp`). Same fix intent, but 1996's approach is more spec-correct and robust against edge-case Accept headers.

clusters.pick_reason: 1996 implements a proper RFC 7231-style Accept header parser (acceptsMediaType): it splits entries on commas, strips per-entry parameters, explicitly excludes entries with q=0, and supports type/subtype wildcard matching. 2046 instead uses a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check with no q-value handling, which can false-positive on unrelated subtypes containing that substring (e.g. `application/json-patch+json`, `application/jsonp`). Same fix intent, but 1996's approach is more spec-correct and robust against edge-case Accept headers.
